correctness.rationale: The degree-d Veronese tangent space at [ell^d] is P(ell^(d-1)V), and its union is the projective image of the corresponding incidence parameter space. Choosing diagonal weights 1,B,...,B^(n-1) with B=d+1 makes all degree-d monomial weights distinct by uniqueness of base-B expansions. Any fixed tangential monomial equals ell^(d-1)m. Since the polynomial ring is a UFD, the irreducible linear form ell dividing a coordinate monomial must be associated to one coordinate variable; total degree d then leaves exactly x_i^d or x_i^(d-1)x_j. The converse is immediate from the tangent-space formula. Thus the fixed locus has n^2 points. Euler localization applies without smoothness, and projectivity yields chi_top=n^2. The packaged checker independently verifies monomial-weight separation and the fixed-monomial classification over a broad finite range.

value.rationale: Tangential Veronese varieties are classical singular varieties that also occur naturally in symmetric tensor geometry. The result computes a canonical global topological invariant uniformly for every source dimension and every Veronese degree at least three. Its degree-independence is structurally non-obvious because the ambient dimension, defining ideal, degree, and singular geometry vary strongly with d. The exact fixed-point description additionally isolates a clean quadratic-to-higher-degree transition in the monomial geometry. This is an all-family structural statement rather than a small or arbitrary parameter slice.
